podcast.body: The album, including "Uprising," was recorded largely at what Muse called Studio Bellini — Matt Bellamy's villa in the village of Moltrasio on Lake Como, Italy, once owned by Italian composer Vincenzo Bellini. George Clooney, Sting, and Richard Branson also have properties in the area. Winston Churchill once lived there and used the villa for painting. The location was also used in *Star Wars: Attack of the Clones* as the planet Naboo. Bellamy later put the two Lake Como apartments on the market for €2.5 million after splitting with his Italian fiancée. "Recorded almost entirely in Matt's villa on Lake Como in Italy."

podcast.body: This album is one of the most critically questioned in Mios's career, although it contains great rock tracks. Critics felt it was an absolute cliché, an attempt to replicate "Absolution's" success, and deepened their characteristic sonic clichés, with an increasingly epic sound, more piano, and Matt Bellamy's increasingly strong vocals. It attempted to be a conceptual album but often featured profound themes that ended up sounding ridiculous. "de resistance" also marked a significant change: the band began self-producing, which is often seen as a mistake for many bands as it can lead to self-referential and repetitive sounds. Despite critical reservations, the album was enjoyed by many, sold well, and features the fantastic three-part "exo-genesis" suite. "Yo creo que desde el punto de la crítica ha sido uno de los albumes más cuestionados a carrega, y es una bega porque es un gran album, tiene grandísimos temazos y es un gran album de rock, pero que no le termino de comenzar a la crítica y yo en parte lo entiendo."
